metadata.content:
KoreLumina Handoff — M49 Autonomous Knowledge Governance Continuation
Mission
Continue KoreLumina as Lead Systems Architect and Principal Engineer.
This is not an MVP. Preserve the existing architecture and complete the autonomous Knowledge Preservation / Governance work without introducing parallel mechanisms, speculative fixes, or governance shortcuts.
The immediate objective is to resolve the remaining 16 legacy Knowledge Packages correctly by determining whether their original evidence can be reprocessed through the current Flow Engine / Knowledge Preservation pipeline, allowing the modern compiler, validation, governance classification, policy execution, and canonical-promotion machinery to determine their proper destination automatically.
Do not manually invent governance identity for these packages.

Non-Negotiable Working Rules


Inspect the repository directly.

GitHub/repository access is available. Do not ask me to paste files that can be inspected directly.


One milestone at a time.

Investigate → establish root cause/contract → implement smallest correct milestone → focused tests → git diff --check → npm run build → user validation → commit/push only after approval.


Do not ask me to manually edit files.

If terminal changes are necessary, provide complete automated commands.


Do not guess field names, contracts, paths, or architecture.

Inspect the current implementation first.


Existing services remain authoritative.

Orchestrate existing production services instead of duplicating their behavior.


Runtime/persisted state is source of truth.


Fail closed on governance uncertainty.

Missing provenance or governance identity must never be fabricated simply to get a package through the pipeline.


Preserve historical lineage.

Do not rewrite history or pretend legacy packages always contained metadata they did not contain.


Do not trigger unrelated systems during certification:


Organizational Memory


Educational admission


Genesis/Day-0 Replay


conversation ingestion

unless the specific milestone explicitly requires them.




Production-grade quality is required.



Current Repository State
Latest locked milestone:
M49 Phase 59 — Durable Governance Exception Classification
commit: 8d6a5e3a50123569f4e09221260573d703f974f9
Phase 59 was committed and pushed.
It introduced:
GovernanceExceptionClassificationService
GovernanceExceptionRecoveryIntegration tests
GovernanceReadyRecoverySweep durable-exception suppression
governance barrel export
focused classifier tests
The classifier records:
metadata.governanceException = {
  type: "incomplete_governance_identity",
  disposition: "manual_reclassification_required",
  source: "legacy_governance_identity_audit",
  recordedAt,
  recordedBy
}
Important: this metadata records why autonomous governance is prohibited. It does not manufacture authority, scope, owner, or version.

Autonomous Governance Architecture Already Completed
The broader M49 work has established autonomous governed processing.
The architecture now includes the existing governed canonical promotion service plus orchestration around it.
Key principle:
Policy decision
    ↓
persisted governed approval
    ↓
autonomous promotion executor
    ↓
GovernedCanonicalPromotionService
    ↓
Canonical Knowledge
GovernedCanonicalPromotionService.promoteApprovedPackage() remains the authoritative canonicalization transition.
It already enforces the package/review/provenance/canonical/manufacturing contracts.
Do not reproduce canonical construction elsewhere.

Runtime Recovery Architecture
Runtime now has event-driven governance processing plus recovery.
The intended operating architecture is:
Governance-ready event
        ↓
Runtime consumer
        ↓
Autonomous Governance Cycle
        ↓
policy/review/promotion machinery
with:
lost event / restart
        ↓
GovernanceReadyRecoverySweep
        ↓
GovernanceReadyRecoveryScheduler
        ↓
same Runtime consumer/orchestrator path
The scheduler runs an immediate startup recovery and subsequently at approximately five-minute intervals.
It has overlap protection, failure isolation, and clean shutdown wiring.

Phase 56
M49 Phase 56 — Governance Recovery Scheduler
Locked at:
4221a16f4dcd700b585b33558dd60a5f19eb5559
The scheduler was integrated into Runtime startup/shutdown.

Phase 57
Startup Recovery Production Certification
Operational certification only; no commit.
The Runtime startup sweep was exercised against real persisted knowledge.
Observed result before legacy quarantine:
scanned: 16
recoverable: 0
recovered: 0
ignored: 0
exceptions: 16
This was correct fail-closed behavior.
All 16 lacked sufficient governance identity.
Existing canonical/adapted knowledge remained unchanged.
The Runtime was subsequently restored and remained healthy.

Phase 58
Legacy Governance Identity Provenance Audit
Read-only operational audit.
The 16 packages were inspected for recoverable persisted governance identity.
Result:
Legacy governance-incomplete packages: 16
Reconstructable from persisted proof: 0
Not reconstructable without inference: 16
The package/item metadata contained no reliable evidence for:
authority
scope
owner
version
classification
Therefore governance identity could not safely be reconstructed directly from those package records.
This was the key reason we refused to assign arbitrary metadata.

Phase 59
Durable Governance Exception Classification
Implemented and locked.
Focused certification was green:
classifier tests: 4/4 passed
recovery integration: 1/1 passed
recovery regression: 9/9 passed
git diff --check: passed
npm run build: passed
The recovery sweep now recognizes a durable:
incomplete_governance_identity
+
manual_reclassification_required
exception and classifies it as ignored rather than repeatedly treating it as a fresh scheduler failure.
It does so before manufacturing-run lookup or governance-consumer invocation.

Phase 60 — Current Operational State
Phase 60 began as a bounded production application of the Phase 59 classifier.
The exact target population was frozen first.
There are exactly 16 legacy packages:
KP-2026-000009
KP-2026-000010
KP-2026-000011
KP-2026-000012
KP-2026-000013
KP-2026-000014
KP-2026-000015
KP-2026-000016
KP-2026-000017
KP-2026-000018
KP-2026-000019
KP-2026-000020
KP-2026-000021
KP-2026-000022
KP-2026-000024
KP-2026-000025
KP-2026-000023 is not part of this population.
All 16 were successfully classified in production.
Every operation returned:
disposition: classified
with:
type:
  incomplete_governance_identity

disposition:
  manual_reclassification_required

source:
  legacy_governance_identity_audit

recordedBy:
  human:founder
and a persisted recordedAt.
No authority, scope, owner, or version was assigned.
No package was approved or promoted.

Important Change in Direction
After classification, we reconsidered whether the user should manually inspect/reclassify all 16.
The answer is: not as the first approach.
The preferable architecture is to determine whether their original source evidence can be reprocessed through the current Flow Engine / Knowledge Preservation pipeline.
The legacy package itself lacks governance identity, but that does not necessarily mean the original source evidence lacks enough semantic/contextual information for the current system to classify it correctly.
Therefore the desired architecture is:
legacy quarantined package
        ↓
resolve original source evidence
        ↓
current Flow Engine / ingestion path
        ↓
current compiler
        ↓
current validation
        ↓
current KnowledgePackageFactory
        ↓
governed replacement Knowledge Package
        ↓
policy resolution
        ↓
autonomous review/promotion if eligible
This is superior to manually assigning:
authority
scope
owner
version
to old package records.

Critical Historical-Preservation Rule
Do not mutate the old package into a modern package.
If reprocessing succeeds:
old legacy package
    ↓
preserved as historical lineage

original evidence
    ↓
reprocessed

new governed package
    ↓
normal modern governance pipeline
Then record an explicit old→new lineage/reprocessing relationship using existing lineage/supersession contracts if they are appropriate.
Do not invent a new lineage model until the existing contracts have been inspected.
The old package should only be marked superseded/reprocessed if the architecture already supports that transition and the replacement has been successfully persisted.

Why These Packages Are Quarantined
They are not known to be bad content.
They are old packages whose persisted records predate the reliable modern governance identity contract.
The system therefore cannot safely answer:
What authority governs this?
What scope does it belong to?
Who owns it?
What version/currentness does it represent?
Which active policy governs it?
The durable exception means:

autonomous policy processing is prohibited until governance identity can be established from trustworthy evidence.

It does not mean:

content is rejected.


Current Question to Resolve
Can the 16 packages be automatically reprocessed through the current Flow Engine so KoreLumina itself determines where they belong?
Likely yes if their original evidence remains resolvable.
That must now be proven directly from the repository and persisted evidence.

Next Milestone
M49 Phase 61 — Legacy Package Flow-Engine Reprocessing Audit
Phase 61 is read-only/investigative first.
Do not immediately reprocess production data.
The goal is to determine, for each of the exact 16 package IDs:


What sourceEvidenceRefs exist?


Can every evidence reference still be loaded from the current evidence store?


What evidence type is it?


What original source location/content reference survives?


Is the underlying source content still resolvable?


Which compiler currently handles that evidence type?


What is the actual modern ingestion/manufacturing entry point?


Does that path naturally reach the current compiler → IR → KnowledgePackageFactory contract?


Does the current compiler derive/propagate:


authority


scope


owner


version


classification

from source/evidence semantics or metadata?




Would reprocessing create a new package safely rather than mutate the old one?


Is there an existing replay/reprocessing/idempotency mechanism that should be reused?


Is there an existing lineage/supersession mechanism appropriate for linking the legacy package to its replacement?


Do not assume all 16 share the same evidence type.

Repository Areas to Inspect Directly
At minimum inspect:
apps/lumina-runtime/src/knowledge-preservation/evidence/
apps/lumina-runtime/src/knowledge-preservation/compiler/
apps/lumina-runtime/src/knowledge-preservation/package/
apps/lumina-runtime/src/knowledge-preservation/manufacturing/
apps/lumina-runtime/src/knowledge-preservation/governance/
apps/lumina-runtime/src/knowledge-preservation/promotion/
apps/lumina-runtime/src/knowledge-preservation/review/
Also search for actual entry points and contracts involving:
sourceEvidenceRefs
EvidenceItem
EvidenceStore
loadEvidence
compiler registry
compile
KnowledgePackageFactory
manufacturing run
reprocess
replay
supersede
supersession
lineage
ingestion
Flow Engine
Do not rely on names from this handoff if the repository uses different names. Inspect actual implementation.

Important Known Contract
Earlier direct inspection established that KnowledgePackageFactory derives governance fields from common IR metadata.
The current compiler path, particularly Documentation compilation, propagates governance fields from evidence metadata into IR.
This is why newly manufactured governed packages work while these old persisted packages do not.
Verify the current implementation again before relying on this statement.

Phase 61 Required Output
Before implementing anything, produce a package-level audit table for the exact 16:
packageId
sourceEvidenceRefs
evidenceResolved
evidenceType
sourceLocation/contentRef
compiler
sourceContentResolvable
modernPipelineEntryPoint
reprocessable
reason
Aggregate:
total = 16
fully reprocessable = N
partially resolvable = N
unresolvable = N
No production mutation during this audit.

If Phase 61 Proves Reprocessing Is Viable
Proceed to a separate implementation milestone:
M49 Phase 62 — Legacy Package Reprocessing Service
Do not combine Phase 61 and 62 unless the architecture is trivial and the user explicitly approves proceeding.
The service should be Runtime-owned and narrowly responsible for orchestration.
Conceptual contract:
legacyPackageId
actorId
Potential result:
legacyPackageId
sourceEvidenceIds
replacementPackageId
manufacturingRunId
disposition
reason
But inspect existing types first. Reuse existing execution identities/contracts if available.
The service must:


Load the exact legacy package.


Verify its durable governance exception.


Resolve its original evidence.


Refuse if evidence is missing/conflicting.


Send evidence through the existing current manufacturing/Flow Engine path.


Never manually construct a canonical record.


Never manually assign governance identity merely to pass policy.


Produce a new package through existing compiler/factory contracts.


Preserve original evidence/provenance.


Record old→new lineage through existing contracts.


Be idempotent.


Never produce duplicate replacement packages on rerun.


Leave the old package intact if reprocessing fails.


Fail one package independently without aborting the others.



Phase 62 Required Tests
At minimum prove:


Legacy package with resolvable evidence produces a replacement package through the existing pipeline.


Replacement package ID is produced by existing package/manufacturing machinery.


Existing compiler is used.


Governance metadata comes from the modern pipeline, not the reprocessing service.


Missing evidence fails closed.


Conflicting evidence fails closed.


Already-reprocessed package is idempotent.


Rerun creates no duplicate replacement.


Old package remains preserved.


Old→new lineage is durable.


Failure of package N does not stop N+1.


No direct canonical construction.


No direct policy creation/modification.


No Organizational Memory adaptation.


No educational admission.


No Genesis/Day-0 Replay.


Aggregate counts equal package-level results.



Production Certification After Phase 62
Do not immediately run all 16.
Use a bounded certification slice first.
Recommended sequence:
1 clearly reprocessable legacy package
        ↓
reprocess
        ↓
inspect replacement package
        ↓
verify governance identity
        ↓
verify provenance
        ↓
verify manufacturing lineage
        ↓
allow normal governance policy processing
        ↓
observe canonical outcome
Only after that is green should the remaining eligible legacy population be processed.
Packages whose source evidence cannot be resolved remain durably quarantined.

Promotion Rule
Do not automatically conclude that all reprocessed packages deserve Canonical Knowledge.
Reprocessing determines what the knowledge is and restores modern governance identity/provenance.
Then the normal governance machinery decides whether it should be:
approved/promoted
held for individual review
blocked
superseded
rejected
otherwise excluded by policy
The reprocessing service must not make that decision itself.

Phase 60 Follow-Up
Phase 60 production classification has already been applied to all 16.
Do not classify them again unless testing idempotency intentionally.
Before beginning Phase 61, verify current Runtime/persisted state directly rather than assuming the process from the previous conversation is still alive.
No source commit should be associated with Phase 60 because it was an operational data change.

Git / Certification Rules
For every source milestone:
focused tests
git diff --check
npm run build
git status --short
Then stop.
Do not commit until I explicitly report/approve green.
After approval:
git add only milestone files
git diff --cached --check
git commit
git push
verify local HEAD == origin branch HEAD
Do not bundle unrelated modifications.

Editing Rules
Terminal-only automated edits when implementation is required.
Do not ask me to open an editor or manually insert snippets.
Recent very long shell blocks caused dquote> problems. Prefer:


short commands;


safe automated Python patches;


Base64 full-file writes where appropriate;


separate implementation/test/build steps.


Do not send enormous fragile shell commands when smaller deterministic steps will work.

Immediate Instruction for the Next Conversation
Start by saying which repository contracts you need to inspect for M49 Phase 61, then inspect them directly through the connected repository.
Do not ask me to run sed, grep, or paste repository files merely so you can understand the architecture.
Do not mutate production state.
Return with the actual evidence-resolution and Flow Engine topology for the 16 quarantined packages and a recommendation on whether a reusable reprocessing service is architecturally justified.
The goal is to complete this entire legacy-package task so that KoreLumina—not the founder manually—can correctly classify and route historical knowledge whenever trustworthy original evidence still exists.
